> Quote one, say which, and use the same one everywhere.

- **Identifier queries (real store)** — of the golds retrieved, 99.7% actually contain the answer; net token economics +519 per recall.

## Temporal cues

This suite is a comparison, not a score: it asks whether phrasing a query with a time
cue ("last week", "in March") helps, and what a working date filter would be worth.

- No temporal cue: **90.1%** s@1 — the baseline.
- Oracle week-filter: **96.0%** — the ceiling a working filter approaches, 5.9pp above baseline.
- Per-phrasing detail in `bench-runs/0.15.9-2026-10-08/temporal.log`. Every cue phrasing currently scores *below* the no-cue baseline, so the cue is not yet being used as a filter.

## Not regenerated by this run

- **Memory Gauntlet (end-to-end ablation).** Lives in the memory-working-agent repo, costs real API spend per arm, and every probe flips between identical runs. Making the probes deterministic is the prerequisite; more reps will not fix it.
- **Production retrieval cost audit.** Reads local Claude Code transcripts, so it measures one operator's usage rather than a property of the release. Re-run deliberately with scripts/measure-claude-vs-awm.ts.
- **LoCoMo.** Retired in 0.13.x: 115-char passages against a real store's ~2,000, one-shot seeding so decay and Hebbian signals contribute nothing, and it rewards indiscriminate retention. Kept only as the record of a tuning decision.

## Reproduce

```bash
npm run bench             # the retrieval fixtures above
npm run bench -- --all    # plus the local challenge suites
```

Raw stdout for every suite is archived under `bench-runs/0.15.9-2026-10-08/`.
